clue.text: New daily direction delaying the attendant

indicators.note: new suggests the word daily is made over into a fresh order of its letters

parts.note: N, north, is a compass direction
delaying means holding back, biding one's time

explanation.surface: A new daily route keeps holding up the servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like the newspaper or a cleaner, but 'New' signals the shuffle of its letters; 'delaying' is the waiting part.
explanation.definitionFit: A noblewoman serving a queen or princess is a personal attendant at court.

clue.text: Sunset in London, when the weed comes out?

explanation.surface: Dusk in the capital is when smokers reach for their tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain vehicle lights had to be on from a set time after sunset; 'the weed' is tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal hour after dusk when vehicle lamps must be switched on; also the moment a smoker sets light to a cigarette.

clue.text: Plunge right in, showing energy

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for plunge

parts.note: to plunge is to dive

explanation.surface: Dive right in to show some vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is vigour and determination, a forceful energy.

clue.text: Divides all constituents, being imprudent

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters of divides all are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Splitting all the voters would be unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters but signals the shuffle of DIVIDES ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwise or rash action is imprudent.

clue.text: Like 1 ac, for instance, in a sickly way holding up the doctor

indicators.note: holding means the word for sickly takes the doctor inside it

parts.note: wanly means palely, sickly

indicators.note: up means the doctor's abbreviation is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Like a lady-in-waiting, sickly enough to hold up the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is the lady-in-waiting, an example of a woman. 'up' turns MO into OM, which WANLY is 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-in-waiting is an example of a female person, so like her means feminine.

clue.text: Temporary one taken in — not in the holidays

indicators.note: taken in means the one is put inside the phrase

parts.note: not in the holidays means during school term, in term
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stopgap appointed during term time, not the vacations.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TERM, the time not in the holidays, has I 'taken in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is provisional, lasting for now.

clue.text: Island feature with halves transposed

indicators.note: with halves transposed means the two pairs of letters swap places

parts.note: a chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: An island landmark with its two parts swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland an inch is a small island; 'with halves transposed' turns CHIN round its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch is a Scottish word for a small isle, as in Inchcolm.

clue.text: Rock used for royal place of worship after great uprising

indicators.note: after means the royal place of worship follows the first piece
uprising means the word for great is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: big means great
R stands for royal, as in RN
an altar is a place of worship

explanation.surface: A stone used to make a royal chapel after a great rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses the word for great, since a down clue reads upwards; 'after' puts the royal place of worship behind it. The Rock is Gibraltar's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is nicknamed the Rock, for its great limestone ridge.

clue.text: Ostracised guard hugs child disturbed by witches

indicators.note: hugs means the guard wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a sentry is a guard

indicators.note: disturbed by means the child is broken open by the witches inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: A sentry, excluded, cuddles a child upset by witches.
explanation.walkthrough: TOT is 'disturbed by' COVEN, giving TOCOVENT, which SENTRY 'hugs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shunned and ignored by everyone is a British idiom for being ostracised.

clue.text: Diver shows remorse, having eaten most of the fruit

indicators.note: having eaten means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: remorse is guilt

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: a lemon is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone who dives into the sea regrets gobbling nearly all the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' sounds like a person but is a diving seabird. 'most of' drops the fruit's last letter, and 'having eaten' puts what is left inside the word for remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird of the auk family hunts fish by diving underwater.

clue.text: Accomplished politician's first message

indicators.note: first here keeps only the opening letter of the politician's short title, discarding the rest

parts.note: a Conservative politician is a Con
accomplished means able, skilled

explanation.surface: A gifted statesman's opening communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'politician's first' takes the opening letter of a short name for a Conservative, an indirect step that older Times clues allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by undersea wire was called a cable, so the word means a sent communication.

clue.text: Leaders of Territorial division crossing very small river

indicators.note: crossing means the two initials sit on either side of the other piece, spanning it
leaders of means the first letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: wee is Scottish for very small

explanation.surface: Commanders of a Territorial Army division cross a tiny stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; its initials T and D straddle WEE ('crossing').
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river on the border of Scotland and England.

clue.text: Eastern drama — jolly type

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese masked drama
a Jolly is naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: An Oriental play features a cheerful character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is not cheerful here: it is old navy slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard or typical pattern can be called a type, the usual model.

clue.text: Temptation to persecute

explanation.surface: An enticement to harass someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is something tempting set out to catch prey; to harass or torment someone is to persecute them, as in bear-baiting.

clue.text: Meandering old player in the Orient

parts.note: a serpent is an obsolete bass wind instrument, something one plays
taken as written
E, east, is the Orient

explanation.surface: An old actor performs in the East, wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' here is a musical instrument, the serpent, not a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding like a snake, a river with many bends is meandering.

clue.text: Cancel appearance of University students if in New York

indicators.note: in means the following pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: L is a learner, so LL stands for students

explanation.surface: University students call off a visit to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: LL is two learners (the L-plate a British learner driver displays), standing for students. 'appearance of' only links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To void or annul something is to cancel it, making it of no effect.

clue.text: Sound philosopher's allegory, say, of one mocked by love?

indicators.note: sound means the following phrase is to be said, not spelt

parts.note: John Locke was the philosopher, and an allegory is an example of a myth, so the phrase is Locke's myth

explanation.surface: An allegory by a sensible thinker, about someone love laughs at?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'sensible' but signals the homophone. The proverb 'love laughs at locksmiths' means no lock keeps lovers apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says love laughs at the craftsmen who fit locks, since lovers always get through.

clue.text: Great conductor from West — eccentric sort

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress, so the surname leads to her first name

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre, odd, so the letters of sort are scrambled

explanation.surface: A celebrated orchestra leader from out West turns out a strange kind of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction: it is Mae West, the film star, giving MAE; 'eccentric' rearranges SORT into STRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished conductor or master musician is honoured with this Italian title.

clue.text: Filthy Lebanese extremists in a French prison

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in means the Lebanese letters go inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is US slang for prison

indicators.note: extremists means the outermost letters of the word Lebanese

explanation.surface: Militants from Lebanon held in a squalid French jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' takes only the outer letters of Lebanese; 'in' puts them inside the American slang word for a prison, after the French for a.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty and impure things are unclean; filth is the strongest form of that.

clue.text: Nymphs in French art supporting the ailing Diana

indicators.note: supporting means the French word sits below the other piece in this down clue
ailing means unwell, so the letters of Diana are put out of order

parts.note: es is French for (thou) art

explanation.surface: Nymphs in French paintings hold up the sick goddess Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb (thou art), French es. 'ailing' rearranges DIANA to NAIAD, which ES is 'supporting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads were water spirits of Greek myth, a kind of nymph.

clue.text: Cockney's horse apt to be put out to grass

indicators.note: to be put out means disturbed, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the h, saying 'orse for horse

explanation.surface: A Londoner's horse is ready to be turned out to pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop initial H, so 'horse' gives ORSE; 'to be put out' shuffles ORSE and APT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough Spanish and North African grass used for making paper and rope.

clue.text: Unpredictable creature disrupting rice production

indicators.note: disrupting means the creature breaks up the rice and the letters are mixed together

parts.note: a rat is a creature

explanation.surface: An erratic beast ruining the rice harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: RAT and RICE are shuffled together; 'production' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irregular and inconsistent is hard to forecast.

clue.text: Nobody leaves to seek an assignment

indicators.note: leaves means the zero goes away from the phrase

parts.note: to seek is to ask for, giving the phrase to ask
nobody is nil, which is O

explanation.surface: No one sets off in search of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' is O (nil), which 'leaves' TO ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work set for someone is an assignment or duty.

clue.text: Mole's equal, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is said, not spelt

parts.note: an equal in rank is a peer

explanation.surface: An animal's counterpart, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is not the animal: it is a stone breakwater or jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a jetty built out into the sea, as a landing stage is.

clue.text: In the kitchen it really replaces salt

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words kitchen it really

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip: this one can stand in for table salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' is only a link; the answer is the salt potassium nitrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, saltpetre, is a chemical salt used in curing meat.

clue.text: He enters the races with a character from Marathon

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the TT, the Tourist Trophy, are the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: He joins the races alongside a runner from Marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; HE 'enters' it, then A. Marathon is in Greece, so a character from there is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the Greek alphabet is a character, the sort used at Marathon in Greece.

clue.text: Hard wood for the steering apparatus

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
elm is a wood

explanation.surface: A tough timber for a ship's steering gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheel or tiller that steers a ship is its helm.

clue.text: Confusion about island's grain

indicators.note: about means the word for confusion surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a maze is a confusing tangle
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Muddle over what an island grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is a cereal crop whose seeds are grain.

clue.text: Injury to people buried in debris — not us

indicators.note: buried in means the people are placed inside the shortened word for debris
not means the letters of us are removed

parts.note: detritus is debris
men are people

explanation.surface: People hurt in the rubble — but none of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not us' strips US from DETRITUS, leaving DETRIT; MEN is 'buried in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or damage done to someone is injury.

clue.text: Minister to whom one may dictate domestically?

definitions.text: Minister to whom one may dictate domestically?

parts.words: Minister to whom one may dictate domestically?
parts.note: read literally, a typist who takes dictation at home; really a senior government minister

explanation.surface: Which minister takes your dictation at home?
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the cabinet minister in charge of domestic affairs, policing and immigration has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet member for internal affairs in Britain is a minister.
